Topics · One God, one message

Who first drew the lines between religions?

The Quran says people began as one and split after knowledge came. It addresses every group, the reader's too.

Part 1 of 4

﴿كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ ۚ وَمَا ٱخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتُ بَغْيًۢا بَيْنَهُمْ ۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لِمَا ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Mankind was [of] one religion [before their deviation]; then Allāh sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between the people concerning that in which they differed. And none differed over it [i.e., the Scripture] except those who were given it - after the clear proofs came to them - out of jealous animosity among themselves. And Allāh guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allāh guides whom He wills to a straight path.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:213

Translation

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,

Acts · 17:26

World English Bible

Before asking who made the separation, ask whether there was one at the start. The verse says people were one community. Then messengers came with the truth to judge between people in what they disputed. And it adds something unexpected: those who differed over the Book were the ones given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. So that split, the verse says, did not come from ignorance. It came from rivalry.

A question for you

When the lines were first drawn, who drew them, in the history as you know it?

If you sayRulers, seeking power
ThenMany Sikh families carry a heavy memory of rulers who used force, and its weight is not denied here. The Quran says there is no compulsion in religion, so whatever was done by force has no support in it.
If you sayPriests and scholars, seeking standing
ThenThe verse says those who differed were the ones given the Book. It points to the learned in every community, and does not exempt the reader's own.
If you sayOrdinary people, out of fear of the other
ThenFear may be part of the story. The verse says clear proofs came first, so the quarrel came after it was known.
If you sayI do not know
ThenAn honest answer. The verses ahead do not ask you to know all of history, only to look at the cause they name.

Part 2 of 4

﴿شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِۦ نُوحًا وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓ ۖ أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ ۚ كَبُرَ عَلَى ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ ۚ ٱللَّهُ يَجْتَبِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ١٣ وَمَا تَفَرَّقُوٓا۟ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ بَغْيًۢا بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى لَّقُضِىَ بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُورِثُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ لَفِى شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ مُرِيبٍ١٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with Allāh is that to which you invite them. Allāh chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]. And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word[1413] that preceded from your Lord [postponing the penalty] until a specified time, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.

Translator's notes

[1413] Decree. See footnote to 10:19.

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:13-14

Translation

for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?

Original · Ancient Greek

ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε. ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;

1 Corinthians · 3:3

World English Bible

The first verse says the religion enjoined on Noah is what was revealed to Muhammad, and enjoined on Abraham, Moses and Jesus too, with one charge: hold the religion upright, and do not split in it. The second says what happened: the split came only after knowledge had reached them, out of rivalry. The order of events is clear: a charge to hold together, then knowledge, then division. The division came after knowing, and with knowing present.

A question for you

The verse says the split came after knowledge. What follows from that?

If you sayPeople split because they did not know
ThenThe verse says otherwise: knowledge had already reached them. If ignorance were the cause, knowledge would have ended it.
If you sayPeople split though they knew
ThenThat is what the verse says. It places the cause in wanting, not in not knowing. So the remedy for division begins inside before it begins outside.
If you sayBoth happen
ThenPerhaps. The verse names the cause of the split, and does not say that every member of any community acted from rivalry.

Part 3 of 4

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَـٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous[1521] of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

Translator's notes

[1521] Literally, "he who has the most taqwā," i.e., consciousness and fear of Allāh, piety and righteousness.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:13

Translation

Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν· Ἐπʼ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ θεός, ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.

Acts · 10:34-35

World English Bible

Is division built into creation? The verse says God made people from a male and a female and made them peoples and tribes. Then it gives the purpose: knowing one another. So difference among peoples and tongues is not the split. It is a road to knowing one another. And honour lies in piety. The verse does not ascribe the divisions among people to God. It ascribes to Him the variety.

A question for you

If the verse gives a reason for the variety among people, which reason would you have guessed?

If you saySo that they would compete
ThenThe verse says otherwise: that you may know one another. Competition in good has its place elsewhere in the Quran. Here the purpose is knowing.
If you saySo that they would know one another
ThenThat is what the verse says. It puts the question before you: what has kept me from knowing the other well enough?
If you sayNo reason, it just happened
ThenMany hold that view. The verse says there is a purpose, and leaves it with you to weigh.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِحَبْلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا۟ ۚ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنتُمْ أَعْدَآءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُم بِنِعْمَتِهِۦٓ إِخْوَٰنًا وَكُنتُمْ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُم مِّنْهَا ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And hold firmly to the rope[142] of Allāh all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allāh upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allāh make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.

Translator's notes

[142] Referring either to His covenant or the Qur’ān.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:103

Translation

See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!

Original · Hebrew

שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד הִנֵּ֣ה מַה־טּ֭וֹב וּמַה־נָּעִ֑ים שֶׁ֖בֶת אַחִ֣ים גַּם־יָֽחַד׃

the Psalms · 133:1

World English Bible

﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا۟ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوا۟ شِيَعًا ۖ كُلُّ حِزْبٍۭ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Or] of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.[1147]

Translator's notes

[1147] Of beliefs, opinions, customs, etc.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:32

Translation

In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes.

Original · Hebrew

בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

Judges · 21:25

World English Bible

The first verse here speaks to Muslims themselves: hold fast together to God's rope and do not divide, and it reminds them they were once enemies and God joined their hearts. The second describes every party: content with what it holds. So the argument points at no single community. It speaks to the reader in whichever community they stand, and to Muslims first. That is what makes it fair.

A question for you

Which communities do these verses speak to?

If you sayOnly the others
ThenThe first verse is addressed to Muslims directly, so it speaks to the Quran's own community first.
If you sayEvery community, including my own
ThenThat is the fair reading. It holds the Muslim to what it holds everyone else, and opens the same way back to all.
If you sayI am not sure
ThenThen take time to read the two verses alone. If you find them addressing one community and not another, say so, and a second reading may change your mind.
